vm_tools: concierge: do not keep xattrs/fflags in VM exports When exporting VMs, do not attempt to store extended attributes or "fflags" (chattr-style attributes). The files that are being archived should be normal files, aside from having the "encrypted" chattr flag set, which can't be preserved in an archive anyway. When libarchive adds files with these flags to a PAX-style tar file, it creates extra sections that GNU tar doesn't understand, which results in confusing error messages when extracting the tarball. Disable them to avoid adding the extra sections when using libarchive's "restricted pax" format so that the resulting tar file is cleanly extract-able with GNU tar and other tar implementations. BUG=chromium:965242 TEST=vmc extract termina termina.tar.gz; tar -xf termina.tar.gz Change-Id: I98893d76e54f964f2371a31b7b376ec4469e0118 Signed-off-by: Daniel Verkamp <dverkamp@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1709036 Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dtor@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Stephen Barber <smbarber@chromium.org>

biod: Mitigate race between powerbutton and fingerprint events. Currently on devices with fingerprint overlapped on power button, behavior of the device can be unpredictable when the user presses powerbutton with an enrolled finger when on lock screen. The behavior depends on the order in which powerd and biod sees the events. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ Order of events as seen by | Current behavior | Expected behavior | biod and powerd | | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ PWRBTN DOWN, PWRBTN UP | Screen turns off | Screen turns off. | FP MATCH | an back on. | Locked. | Initial state: screen on | Unlocked. | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ PWRBTN DOWN, FP MATCH | Screen turns off | Screen turns off. | PWRBTN UP | Unlocked. | Locked. | Initial state: screen on | | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ PWRBTN DOWN, FP MATCH | Screen turns on | Screen turns on. | PWRBTN UP | Unlocked. | Locked. | Initial state: screen off | | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ FP MATCH, PWRBTN DOWN, | Screen turns off | Screen turns off. | FP MATCH | Unlocked. | Locked. | | | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ This is a fix to address the first 3 scenarios. In this CL, we listen for power button down/up events from powerd. If we see these events in last |kAuthIgnoreTimeoutmsecs|, we assume that fp match is an side effect of user interacting with the power button. Thus we ignore the match. BUG=b:118713688 TEST=manual, deploy on nocturne and test 1 & 2 are fixed. Change-Id: Ia286921236db5232d092eefdd7d90065ef4c48e8 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1540946 Tested-by: Ravi Chandra Sadineni <ravisadineni@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Ravi Chandra Sadineni <ravisadineni@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Nicolas Norvez <norvez@chromium.org>

hwid: Remove chassis from default encoding and increase RO EC field length The 'chassis' was introduced after Reef (multi-OEM zerg) and before Unibuild (Coral). It had few assumptions that are no longer true today, for example: - `chassis` was designed to support multiple projects (zerg or WL) in a single HWID database file, but follower units are now always identified as new 'model' today which has its own HWID database file. - Since Unibuild, the 'chassis' is always reported as model name. - Since Unibuild, white label units share same chassis name. So what it served was replaced by either model name or SKU information. Given all newer projects will only do Unibuild, we should release the 5 bits for better usage. In the meantime, we previously allocated 3 bits for AP RO firmware, and 2 for EC RO. These were not sufficient because devices may have 2~3 unsupported RO (EVT, DVT, PVT) and 2~3 times of refresh, so in the end we often see devices increasing fields for these, making it harder to search and maintain, for example counting EC RO field length: nocturne(3), shyvana(3), grabbiter(3), sand(6), apel(3), eve(6), atlas(6), dumo(4), robo(4), wukong(7), ..... So let's try to make it default to 5 bits now. Note that dram, ap/ec RO fw version and fw key fields have moved to different location. Devices with existing HWID database file do not need to change anything. This is simply changing the default new file created by HWID database builder.
